newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU states disagree over grain base area penalties.
newsitem.headline: EU states disagree over grain base area penalties.

text.p: European Union member states are blocking plans to introduce rules on applying penalties for overplanting cereals, an EU diplomat said on Thursday.
The European Commission has put forward a proposal, based on German demands, to allow penalties for exceeding annual base area planting to be targeted at the regions responsible.
Currently member states whose farmers exceed base area limits for cereals face a one percent cut in aid for every one percent of overplanting.
In July the Commission waived a second penalty applying a similar cut in the base area.
The proposed change followed a German request made because some of their Laender (states) felt that penalties should only apply to those states which exceeded the base area limits.

"This is an ongoing discussion in the special agriculture committee. As always happens, it is being held up because some national officials are arguing for measures to limit the impact on their own cereal farmers," the EU diplomat said.
